title: The Plans Practice in Context

header.html: Apply the plans practice: plan levels (project, stage, team, exception), project product description, work package description; areas of focus of key roles; effective planning and techniques; analyze whether a planning approach is effective and fit for purpose considering the principles, the techniques and tailoring
the official PRINCE2 7 Practitioner syllabus (PeopleCert, version 7.2)

toc.title: Areas of focus of the key roles

html:
1Purpose, objectives and principles

The plans practice supports communication and control. A plan says what will be delivered, how, when, by whom and at what cost. Once the right level approves it, the plan becomes the baseline that progress is measured against.

The practice serves these principles: focus on products (plan from the products, not from tasks), manage by stages (detail only for the stage ahead), manage by exception (tolerances sit inside the plan), learn from experience (past lessons feed estimates) and continued business justification (plan cost and time feed the business case).

Exam tip

. Match the plan to the management level. The board approves the project plan, stage plans and exception plans. The team manager owns the team plan. A scenario that gives the wrong person the wrong level of plan is a red flag.

2The key management products

Product What it is for
Project plan The whole project: major products, stages, cost, time, quality; updated at each stage boundary
Stage plan One management stage in detail. Prepared by the project manager near the end of the previous stage; approved by the board
Team plan An optional plan prepared by a team manager to deliver work packages, often in the team's own format
Exception plan A plan that replaces the rest of the current plan when a tolerance is forecast to be exceeded; the board requests it and approves it
Project product description What the project as a whole must deliver, with the user quality expectations and acceptance criteria; agreed before detailed planning
Work package description The work, product, standards, tolerances and reporting that the project manager agrees with a team manager before work starts
Exam tip

. Work package description goes down to the team manager; exception plan goes up to the board. An exception plan replaces what remains of the current plan; it is not an addition.

3Areas of focus of the key roles

Role Focus in the plans practice
Executive Plans stay affordable and consistent with the business case
Senior user Plans deliver what users need; agrees the project product description and acceptance criteria
Senior supplier Plans are achievable with the supplier's resources and estimates
Project manager Prepares project, stage and exception plans; writes work package descriptions
Team manager Prepares team plans; agrees work packages and estimates
Project assurance Checks plans are realistic and follow standards
Project support Helps with planning tools, estimating data and plan upkeep

Where you are unsure of a detail, the exam habit is to check the book's table.

4Effective planning and techniques

The planning approach is the agreed way of planning on this project: how many levels of plan, which tools, which estimating method and which standards. The syllabus names no separate product for it.

Technique What good looks like
Product-based planning Write the project product description, draw the product breakdown structure, write product descriptions, draw the product flow diagram. Then find activities and dependencies
Estimating Made with the people who will do the work, using past data and lessons; assumptions are stated
Scheduling Uses dependencies and resource availability to show when, and the critical path
Tolerances Set for the aspects of performance: corporate level sets project tolerance, the board sets stage tolerance, the project manager sets work package tolerance
Planning horizon Detail for the current stage; outline for later stages
The plan as a control The approved plan is the baseline; forecasts are compared with it

On Project Harbor a typical stage tolerance is plus or minus 10% cost and two weeks time.

Exam tip

. Products first, activities second. If a plan starts with a task list and no product descriptions, it is not product-based planning, and acceptance criteria are probably missing.

5Judging a scenario

An effective approach Red flags (not fit for purpose)
Outline project plan; detailed plan for the current stage only (manage by stages) Detailed plans for every stage drawn up at the start and treated as fixed
Plans start from products and their descriptions (focus on products) A task list with no products, quality criteria or acceptance criteria
Every plan carries tolerances set by the level above (manage by exception) A single fixed date and cost, so every small slip goes to the board
Work package matches the stage plan and is agreed with the team manager Work starts on a verbal request, or the work package quietly changes scope
Forecast breach: exception report, then an exception plan if the board asks Project manager hides the breach, stretches the stage or writes a new plan unasked
Estimates made with the doers and past lessons (learn from experience) Estimates guessed by one person or never revisited
Project plan updated at each stage boundary and re-approved Project plan never updated after approval

Tailoring.

Context How planning changes
Small internal project One combined plan; no team plan; short descriptions; decision recorded
Agile or hybrid delivery Stage plan keeps time, cost and tolerances; sprint or release plans give the detail; scope flexes inside acceptance criteria
Large or multi-party project Team plans for each supplier; dependencies between suppliers planned and integrated
Sustainability or data concerns Plan includes sustainability and data measures and their tolerances
Exam tip

. Tailoring changes the form of a plan, not the need for one. An answer that drops tolerances, baselines or board approval of stage plans because the project is small or agile is wrong.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1In Project Harbor, the build stage has a cost tolerance of plus or minus 10%. Sam Okafor forecasts a 14% overspend, drops the testing activities to recover the cost and carries on without telling anyone. Was this appropriate for the project manager?

  • AYes, because the project manager owns the stage plan and may change its activities freely
  • BYes, because dropping the testing activities brings the forecast back inside the tolerance
  • CNo, because the forecast breach must go to the board, which can request an exception plan
  • DNo, because only a team manager has the authority to change activities in a stage plan
Show the answer

Answer: C. Manage by exception requires the forecast breach to be reported so the board decides; the plan cannot be quietly rewritten.

S2Project Harbor's initiation stage is ending. Sam Okafor is tempted to plan the build, pilot and rollout stages in full detail so the board feels certain. What should he do?

  • APlan the build stage in detail and keep the later stages in outline in the project plan
  • BPlan all three stages in detail now and baseline them so the board has full certainty
  • CPlan the build stage in detail and leave the pilot and rollout stages out of the project plan
  • DAsk the team manager to plan all three stages in detail and attach them to the project plan
Show the answer

Answer: A. Manage by stages and the planning horizon call for detail only for the next stage, with later stages in outline in the project plan.

S3Sam Okafor is about to authorize the next piece of build work to Wei Chen's team. Who is responsible for preparing the work package description that sets out the work, the product and the tolerances?

  • AWei Chen, the team manager
  • BLena Kovac, the senior supplier
  • CAisha Bello, project assurance
  • DSam Okafor, the project manager
Show the answer

Answer: D. The project manager prepares the work package description and agrees it with the team manager, who does not write the description of their own assignment.

S4Tomas Reyes wants the acceptance criteria for the whole online permit service agreed before the detailed plan is built. Which management product records them?

  • AWork package description
  • BProject product description
  • CStage plan and its schedule
  • DTeam plan of the supplier
Show the answer

Answer: B. The project product description holds what the whole project must deliver and the acceptance criteria; the others cover work, a stage or a team.

S5Sam Okafor sends Wei Chen a work package as an email with a task list and a due date only. There are no quality criteria, tolerances or reporting arrangements. Was this appropriate?

  • AYes, because a task list and a due date are enough to hold the supplier to account for results
  • BYes, because Wei Chen's team already knows the supplier's standards and needs no tolerances
  • CNo, because it must state the product, quality criteria, tolerances and reporting and be agreed
  • DNo, because the project board must approve every work package before it is issued to a team
Show the answer

Answer: C. A work package is a controlled agreement on product, standards, tolerances and reporting; a bare task list leaves both sides guessing.

S6Wei Chen's team delivers Project Harbor's build stage in two-week sprints from a prioritized backlog. What should Sam Okafor do about the stage plan?

  • AReplace the stage plan with the product backlog and drop the stage tolerances for the stage
  • BKeep a stage plan with time, cost and tolerances, with sprint plans giving the detail
  • CAsk Wei Chen to plan every sprint in the stage in full detail before the stage can start
  • DHand the planning of the stage entirely to the team and stop reporting against any plan
Show the answer

Answer: B. Tailoring adapts the form of planning for agile delivery, but the stage plan, tolerances and board control stay in place.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What does an exception plan replace?

Show the answer

The remainder of the current plan, after a tolerance is forecast to be exceeded and the board asks for it.

R2What is the first step of product-based planning?

Show the answer

Write the project product description.

R3Who sets the tolerance for a work package?

Show the answer

The project manager, for the team manager.

R4Which plan is optional and prepared by a team manager?

Show the answer

The team plan.

R5How far ahead is detailed planning done in a staged project?

Show the answer

For the current stage only; later stages stay in outline.

R6What does a work package description tell a team manager?

Show the answer

The work to do, the product to deliver, the standards, tolerances and reporting.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Plan levels project plan, stage plan, team plan, exception plan
Exception plan replaces the rest of a plan when tolerance is forecast to be exceeded; board requests and approves
Project product description what the whole project delivers, with acceptance criteria
Work package description project manager to team manager: work, product, tolerances, reporting
Product-based planning products first, then activities, estimates and schedule
Tolerances corporate sets project, board sets stage, project manager sets work package
Tailoring changes the form of plans, never drops tolerances or approval
